learning_outcomes.text: Know the fundamental concepts and current legislation in industrial safety.
Identify and evaluate risks in industrial facilities, production processes, work environments, and machinery.
Address design problems from the industrial safety perspective.
Know the fire protection actions and measures applicable in industrial buildings and facilities.
Know the minimum safety provisions applicable to machinery and work equipment for their commercialization, use, and commissioning.
Identify existing risks and their prevention measures during work in confined spaces, explosive atmospheres, legionella-generating installations, and during terrestrial transport of dangerous goods.

assessment_rules: The course is evaluated through continuous assessment: a partial exam (50%), practices (25%), and a final practical work with presentation (25%). A minimum of 4 out of 10 points on the partial exam is required to average with the practices and final work. Alternatively, students can opt for a final exam covering all contents (30% theoretical, 70% practical), requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 points to pass. The optional COIL activity can replace the final practical work, maintaining its 25% weight.
